subject: Chemistry
description: Ore extraction, roasting, calcination, blast furnace, froth flotation, electrolysis

questions.stem: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust is:
questions.explanation: Earth's crust composition by mass (order): Oxygen (46%), Silicon (28%), Aluminium (8.2%), Iron (5.6%), Calcium, Sodium, Potassium, Magnesium. Aluminium is the most abundant metal and 3rd most abundant element overall. Its chief ore is bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O); extracted by Hall-Héroult electrolysis (1886). Very reactive — does NOT occur in free state, only as oxide.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The process of heating a sulphide ore strongly in presence of excess air — below its melting point — to convert it into an oxide is called:
questions.explanation: Roasting — sulphide ore + O₂ → metal oxide + SO₂. Example: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂. Applied to sulphide ores (galena PbS, zinc blende ZnS, copper pyrites CuFeS₂). Calcination — heat a carbonate / hydrated oxide in absence of air (limestone CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂). Smelting = reduction in a blast furnace. Leaching = dissolving the ore in a suitable solvent.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: In the extraction of iron from haematite in a blast furnace, the reducing agent that actually reduces iron(III) oxide is:
questions.explanation: Though coke is the fuel, the actual reducing agent in most reactions is CO (not C). Blast furnace reactions (top to bottom): Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ (main reduction, 500-900 °C); C + CO₂ → 2CO (Boudouard reaction regenerates CO); C + O₂ → CO₂ at the tuyeres. Limestone decomposes — CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ — then CaO + SiO₂ (silica gangue) → CaSiO₃ slag, separates from molten iron.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: 'Froth flotation' is a concentration technique used primarily for:
questions.explanation: Froth flotation separates sulphide ores (CuFeS₂, ZnS, PbS) from gangue. Ore is ground, mixed with water, pine oil (frothing agent) and xanthate (collector). Compressed air creates froth; sulphide particles — being hydrophobic — attach to the oil-coated bubbles and float. Hydrophilic gangue sinks. Basis — difference in wettability. Widely used in India's Kolar gold mines and Hindustan Zinc operations.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Aluminium is commercially extracted from bauxite by:

options.option_text: Reduction with coke in blast furnace
Electrolysis of molten alumina dissolved in cryolite

questions.explanation: Hall-Héroult process (1886): pure Al₂O₃ (from Bayer process) is dissolved in molten cryolite Na₃AlF₆ at ~950 °C (cryolite lowers alumina's melting point from 2050 °C). Electrolysis — carbon anodes, steel cathode. Cathode: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. Anode: O²⁻ ions oxidise, gradually consuming the carbon anodes (2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻; C + O₂ → CO₂). Very energy-intensive — major users are near hydro power.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The substance added to an ore during smelting to remove siliceous (SiO₂) impurities is a:
questions.explanation: Flux — an added substance that reacts with impurities to form fusible 'slag' separable from molten metal. Rule: pair acid-base opposites. Silica (SiO₂) is acidic → use basic flux (limestone CaCO₃ / CaO) → CaSiO₃ slag. If ore's gangue is basic (CaO, FeO) → use acidic flux (SiO₂) → silicate slag. Slag is less dense, floats on molten metal, easy to tap off separately.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Match the ore with its metal — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is an ore of ALUMINIUM, not copper. Chief copper ore is chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂). Common ore-metal pairs: haematite Fe₂O₃ — Fe; magnetite Fe₃O₄ — Fe; bauxite Al₂O₃·2H₂O — Al; galena PbS — Pb; cinnabar HgS — Hg; zinc blende ZnS — Zn; malachite Cu₂(OH)₂CO₃ — Cu. Remembering the formula colour/name usually gives the element away.
